metadata.name: Riyad as-Salihin (selection)
metadata.translator: Primary: Riyad us-Saliheen, English translation by Hafiz Salahuddin Yusuf (Darussalam), distributed free for da'wah on islamhouse.com and islamicfoundation.ie (hadith 1-5, 7-9, 11-12). Hadith 6 (mercy) and 10 (gentleness): Encyclopedia of Translated Prophetic Hadiths (hadeethenc.com), a free da'wah translation project.

hadiths.text: Verily, Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His slave than a person who has his camel in a waterless desert carrying his provision of food and drink and it is lost. He, having lost all hopes (to get that back), lies down in shade and is disappointed about his camel; when all of a sudden he finds that camel standing before him. He takes hold of its reins and then out of boundless joy blurts out: 'O Allah, You are my slave and I am Your Rubb'. He commits this mistake out of extreme joy. (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 15, narrated by Anas; Al-Bukhari and Muslim — Muslim's wording quoted here)

How wonderful is the case of a believer; there is good for him in everything and this applies only to a believer. If prosperity attends him, he expresses gratitude to Allah and that is good for him; and if adversity befalls him, he endures it patiently and that is better for him. (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 27, narrated by Suhaib bin Sinan; Muslim)

Truth leads to piety and piety leads to Jannah. A man persists in speaking the truth till he is enrolled with Allah as a truthful. Falsehood leads to vice and vice leads to the Fire (Hell), and a person persists on telling lies until he is enrolled as a liar. (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 54, narrated by Abdullah bin Mas'ud; Agreed upon — Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

Nothing will be heavier on the Day of Resurrection in the Scale of the believer than good manners. Allah hates one who utters foul or coarse language. (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 626, narrated by Abud-Darda; At-Tirmidhi)

A person came to Messenger of Allah (PBUH) and asked, "Who among people is most deserving of my fine treatment?'' He (PBUH) said, "Your mother". He again asked, "Who next?'' "Your mother'', the Prophet (PBUH) replied again. He asked, "Who next?'' He (the Prophet (PBUH)) said again, "Your mother.'' He again asked, "Then who?'' Thereupon he (PBUH) said, "Then your father.'' (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 316, narrated by Abu Hurairah; Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

Those who are merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to the inhabitants of earth and the One in the heaven will be merciful to you. (narrated by 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr; Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi and Ahmad — graded Authentic. Quoted from the free Encyclopedia of Translated Prophetic Hadiths, hadeethenc.com.)
The strong man is not one who is good at wrestling, but the strong man is one who controls himself in a fit of rage. (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 45, narrated by Abu Hurairah; Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

If you all depend on Allah with due reliance, He would certainly give you provision as He gives it to birds who go forth hungry in the morning and return with full belly at dusk. (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 79, narrated by 'Umar; At-Tirmidhi)

A man set out to visit a brother (in Faith) in another town and Allah sent an angel on his way. When the man met the angel, the latter asked him, "Where do you intend to go?'' He said, "I intend to visit my brother in this town.'' The angel said, "Have you done any favour to him?'' He said, "No, I have no desire except to visit him because I love him for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, and Glorious.'' Thereupon the angel said, "I am a messenger to you from Allah (to inform you) that Allah loves you as you love him (for His sake)". (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 361, narrated by Abu Hurairah; Muslim)

O 'Aishah, indeed, Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness, and He gives for gentleness what He does not give for violence and what He does not give for anything else. (narrated by 'Aishah; Sahih Muslim 2593 — graded Authentic. Quoted from the free Encyclopedia of Translated Prophetic Hadiths, hadeethenc.com.)
Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother (Muslim) with a cheerful face. (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 121, narrated by Abu Dharr; Muslim)
Whosoever gives me a guarantee to safeguard what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I shall guarantee him Jannah. (Riyad us-Saliheen No. 1513, narrated by Sahl bin Sa'd; Al-Bukhari)
